findings.finding: Bootstrap ordering of the seed files. The catalog does not exist at the merge-base of the very diff that adds it, so by the spec's own rule ("only the base catalog counts"), none of the six seeded testkit files can be classified as infra in this change. If any of those six files is touched in this same iterate (likely, since the gate code and the tests live nearby), the gate will flag its tests as untagged/bad-infra-class and the iterate may be unmergeable as a single change.
findings.suggestion: Either confirm none of the six seed files is touched in this diff, or explicitly sequence: merge 1 = catalog + marker registration + gate code; merge 2 = touch/retag the seed files. State this in the mini-plan so the builder isn't surprised.

findings.finding: Module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.covers_none(...)` classifies every test in the file as infra. This is per the spec, but a file in the catalog that later gains a genuinely new requirement test would have that test silently absorbed into infra (no `covers` → no contradiction, path is in base catalog → granted). The gate only reacts on touch, so the new test never gets flagged as needing a `covers` tag.
findings.suggestion: Consider having the `bad-infra-class`/grant message (or the CI catalog validator) note when a catalog file uses module-level `pytestmark` form, so reviewers know new tests added there need explicit `covers` to opt out. At minimum document this in `conventions.md`.

findings.finding: Digest-ignoring `covers_none` interacts with the "moved tagged test" correction: a test moved to a catalog file and given the marker matches the base digest (digest ignores the marker), which is handled — but the same digest mechanism means a deleted-and-re-added-in-place test with the marker added is judged as a correction, not as a new infra test. That path is covered by the correction rule's constraints, but it's worth an explicit test that a correction whose base path is also outside the base catalog is refused (spec implies it; test list only has "outside base catalog" for the plain case).
findings.suggestion: Add the test: moved base-tagged test + `covers_none` + base path not in catalog → `bad-infra-class`.

findings.finding: None` catalog → "cannot enforce". Depending on how the gate's `read()` returns `None` (unreadable vs. absent-at-base), every merge whose base predates the catalog could return `None` rather than `""`, making the gate report "cannot enforce" for the entire historical timeline of the repo. The spec distinguishes `""` (absent) from `None` (unreadable), but whether `read(path, "base")` can distinguish these for a path that never existed in git history depends on the existing helper's semantics.
findings.suggestion: Verify empirically what `read()` returns for a path absent at base; if it returns `None`, map absent-at-base to the `""` (empty, silent) case explicitly, since "cannot enforce" should mean a real read failure, not a file that predates the feature.

findings.finding: Marker registration "wherever `covers` is registered" is described as a check, not an enumerated list. If a consumer template or vendored plugin `pyproject.toml` is missed, strict-marker runs break in downstream repos, not in this repo's CI — the failure surfaces late.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the registration sites in the mini-plan (grep output for `covers` in `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`pytest.ini` across repo + `shared/templates`) so the builder has a concrete checklist rather than a search task.

findings.finding: The exemption-share denominator change ("infra ids leave `v.touched`") could shift an existing run's exemption share across a threshold, flipping previously-green merges that combine exemptions with infra tests in the same diff. This is semantically correct but is a behavior change to an existing gate output that some goldens may pin.
findings.suggestion: Check whether any golden/freeze tests pin the F11 summary line or exemption share; update goldens deliberately, not as a surprise diff.

findings.finding: Step 1 contradicts the digest acceptance criterion. It proposes skipping both `pytest.mark.covers_none` and `mark.covers_none`, while the specification permits ignoring only the exact `pytest.mark.covers_none` shape. An alias decorator would consequently stop counting as a body edit.
findings.suggestion: Separate marker detection from digest filtering. Detect aliases for validation, but exclude only the exact `pytest.mark.covers_none` decorator from the digest. Add a regression test proving that adding `mark.covers_none` changes the digest.

findings.finding: Step 3 adds valid infrastructure tests to `v.infra` only when they already have an `untagged-added` or `untagged-modified` finding. Valid stand-in corrections and unchanged infrastructure tests in a changed file can therefore pass validation without being counted consistently or removed from `v.touched`.
findings.suggestion: Classify every successfully validated infrastructure test in the dedicated pass, including accepted corrections. Separately remove any superseded untagged finding. Test the reported count and exemption denominator for each case.

findings.finding: Contradiction detection describes assignment forms but does not explain resolving referenced marker values. For example, `requirement_marks = [pytest.mark.covers("AC55")]` followed by `pytestmark = requirement_marks` applies a requirement marker without placing a `.covers` attribute directly inside the `pytestmark` assignment. A syntax-only scan of that assignment could incorrectly grant infrastructure status.
findings.suggestion: Resolve local marker references used by applicable `pytestmark` assignments, or reject unresolved expressions when granting infrastructure status. Cover module and class references in tests.  The base-catalog approach is sound and the scope is appropriate. Resolve these parser and classification inconsistencies before implementation so the gate enforces the stated contract consistently.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the change does not alter the gate's behaviour for changes that do not reclassify anything — _refuse_quiet_loss also fired for infra tests already honoured at base when an unrelated requirement test was retired in the same change, with a misleading 'do not reclassify' message.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a catalog edited in the same change licenses nothing — _merge_base can fall back to the branch's upstream when origin/HEAD is unset, so a pushed earlier commit that widens the catalog becomes the base. A weakness of the shared merge-base resolver, not of this change.
findings.suggestion: DISCLOSED: inherited from the resolver every F11 gate uses; the shipwright flow branches off a freshly fetched origin default branch; CODEOWNERS is the backstop.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a bad catalog fails closed harmlessly — A catalog with one invalid entry is empty as a whole; removing an entry while its file still declares covers_none would self-lock that file's next edit.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: covers_none cannot be used to dodge a requirement tag — A new untagged test appended to a file with a module-level marker was classed automatically.
findings.suggestion: RESOLVED: a test new at head needs its own function/class-level marker; the module-level marker only classes tests already in the file. Tests added; AC55 reworded.

findings.finding: The Design Notes say the catalog is seeded with the six existing testkit meta-test files, but no catalog file is created in this diff; the head-catalog CI test (`test_the_head_catalog_is_valid_and_names_existing_files`) self-skips while the file is absent, and the CODEOWNERS line guards a path that does not yet exist. The glm bootstrap review notes say this deferral is deliberate ("no seed file is touched in this run; retag is a follow-up merge"), so this is a disclosed deviation rather than a hole — the bootstrap test `test_without_a_catalog_at_base...` proves nothing is granted meanwhile.
findings.suggestion: Ship as-is, but make sure the follow-up merge that creates the seed catalog is actually tracked; otherwise the "guarded by CODEOWNERS" claim is vacuous until then.

findings.finding: _correction` appends the "drops stand-in tag" WARNING the moment a correction is accepted, but `_refuse_quiet_loss` runs afterwards and can demote the same test to `bad-infra-class` (e.g. an unrelated tagged test vanished in the same change). The gate output then simultaneously reports a hard finding for the test and a WARNING that it "drops stand-in tag (reclassified as infrastructure)" — contradictory/misleading operator output.
findings.suggestion: Move the warning emission to after `_refuse_quiet_loss`, or have `_refuse_quiet_loss` retract the warnings belonging to tests it demotes.

findings.suggestion: Optional: run the sibling check before the module-level check, or aggregate both reasons.

findings.finding: This case is only asserted against `py_infra_info` directly, not through `evaluate` like the other contradiction forms; a wiring mistake in `_verdict`'s `info.bad` consumption would not be caught by it. The remaining forms are covered end-to-end, so the residual risk is small.
findings.suggestion: Route one of the four parametrized cases through `_run`/`evaluate` as well. findings.finding: Scope-marker parsing ignores assignment targets other than a plain name. For example, `pytestmark, unused = ([mark.covers("FR-01.11")], None)` applies a requirement marker in pytest, but this parser overlooks it and can grant a function’s `covers_none` declaration. This misses the required contradiction check across all assignment forms.
findings.suggestion: Handle destructuring and subscript assignments involving `pytestmark`, or conservatively refuse infrastructure classification when such assignments cannot be resolved. Add tests using these forms with a direct `covers_none` decorator.

findings.finding: An unreadable base catalog produces `catalog=None`, but the gate continues. Only tests declaring `covers_none` subsequently fail; a change without those declarations can pass without reporting “cannot enforce.” The specification explicitly distinguishes unreadable catalogs from absent or invalid ones.
findings.suggestion: Return a “cannot enforce” failure immediately when the base catalog read returns `None`. Add a gate-level test for an unreadable catalog with no infrastructure declarations.

findings.finding: Catalog validation accepts any relative `.py` path, and the new head-catalog test checks only that the file exists. Consequently, an existing production file such as `shared/scripts/example.py` passes the promised CI validation even though it is not a test file.
findings.suggestion: Extend head-catalog validation to verify that each entry identifies a test file under the repository’s collection rules. Add a negative test using an existing non-test Python file.  Ship-with-fixes. The implementation covers the main classification flow, but assignment parsing and catalog enforcement leave concrete acceptance criteria incomplete.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
